label: prf:q-exponential-taylor
title: Proof of q exponential taylor
html:
Proof. The categorical defining equation D_q\, \exp_q = \exp_q, joined with the boundary condition \exp_q(0) = 1, determines a unique formal power series \exp_q(x) = \sum_{n\ge 0} a_n x^n in R[\![x]\!]. The Jackson derivative acts on monomials via D_q(x^n) = [n]_q\, x^{n-1}. We substitute this into the equation:

  D_q\,\sum_n a_n x^n
  \;=\; \sum_{n \ge 0} a_n [n]_q x^{n-1}
  \;=\; \sum_{m \ge 0} a_{m+1} [m+1]_q x^m.

Equating this to \sum_m a_m x^m forces the recursion a_{m+1} = a_m / [m+1]_q. With a_0 = 1, we obtain:

  a_n \;=\; \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{[k]_q} \;=\; \frac{1}{[n]_q!}.

This verifies the claimed coefficient. Convergence on a neighbourhood of 0 holds because [n]_q! \to \infty faster than geometrically when |q| < 1 or |q| > 1. When |q| = 1, write q = e^{2\pi i\theta}; for irrational \theta convergence holds by Diophantine estimates on \theta. This series provides the archimedean realisation of the universal grouplike. Its existence over \mathbb{C} forms a theorem about the \mathbb{C}-fibre of the moduli of grouplikes over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], not a redefinition of \exp_q. \qed

Special values.

Regime [n]_q! asymptotic \exp_q(x) behaviour
q = 1 n! (classical) \exp_q(x) = e^x (ordinary exponential)
0 < q < 1 (1 - q)^{-n}\,n!\,(1 + O(q^n)) slow-growth; radius \infty
q > 1 q^{\binom{n}{2}}\,n!_{q^{-1}} faster-than-classical growth
q \to \infty q^{\binom{n}{2}} entire, type \log q

Relation to physical constants. Evaluating at the QOU substrate value q_0 (local substrate q) yields e_{q_0}(x) = \sum x^n / [n]_{q_0}!. This series generates the moments of the Reeb-flow distribution on \mathcal{S}. Because [n]_{q_0}! \sim q_0^{\binom{n}{2}} n!_{q_0^{-1}} grows super-exponentially at q_0 \approx 1.11, the series converges for all x \in \mathbb{C}. The q-heat kernel and its Gaussian core (q-Gaussian solves the q-heat equation) are therefore well-defined at the physical value of q, avoiding any |q| \le 1 restriction.
